strategies.summary: Trade only when higher-timeframe conditions are one-sided with an obvious draw on liquidity. Stand aside in 50/50 conditions, right after a major expansion has taken the draw on liquidity, and before CPI, FOMC or NFP releases.

timeframes.notes: Requires higher timeframe context (4-hour and above) to establish the obvious draw on liquidity.

glossary.Clear One-Sidedness: When you can only make arguments on one side of the market (e.g., 100% bullish, 0% bearish) with no opposing PD arrays or structure.
glossary.50/50 Bias: When both bullish and bearish arguments exist (even if weighted 70/30 or 90/10), making the market low probability.
glossary.Low Probability Conditions: A state where the odds are not heavily in your favor, commonly occurring during 50/50 biases, after major expansions hit a target, or ahead of major news.

custom_signals.name: obvious_draw_on_liquidity
custom_signals.plain_definition: A higher-timeframe target that is recognisable within about 10 seconds of opening the chart.

custom_signals.name: failed_rejection
custom_signals.plain_definition: Price sweeps a level but does not displace away from it immediately, drifting instead.
custom_signals.numeric_definition: count(structural_event.kind == liquidity_sweep_low, K_REACTION_WINDOW_CANDLES + 1) > count(structural_event.kind == liquidity_sweep_low, K_REACTION_WINDOW_CANDLES) AND NOT any(custom_signals.displacement_candle, K_REACTION_WINDOW_CANDLES)

custom_signals.name: displacement_candle
custom_signals.plain_definition: A strong expansion candle in the trade direction.
custom_signals.numeric_definition: close > open AND body >= K_DISPLACEMENT_BODY_MULT * avg(body[-1], K_DISPLACEMENT_LOOKBACK)

custom_signals.name: consolidation_expansion_consolidation
custom_signals.plain_definition: Three-candle rhythm: consolidation (or expansion), an expansion candle that creates a fair value gap, then an unpredictable consolidation candle.

custom_signals.name: major_expansion_dol_swept
custom_signals.plain_definition: A major expansion has just taken out the higher-timeframe draw on liquidity.

custom_signals.name: pre_major_news
custom_signals.plain_definition: The part of a CPI, FOMC or NFP release day before the release time.

invalidation.text: If you need to convince yourself to take the trade or force the price action, the setup is invalid.
If price sweeps a level but fails to immediately reject and instead slowly climbs/drops, it becomes a 50/50 bias and is invalid.

filters.text: Do not trade ahead of CPI, FOMC, and NFP; wait until after the release.
Do not chase price or try to call a top/bottom immediately after a major expansion has taken the draw on liquidity. Wait for clear 4H+ structure.

entry_rule.text: Wait for price to deliver exactly to your pre-planned 'if/then' demands based on the obvious draw on liquidity.
entry_rule.quote: demanding something off of price and price doing exactly what you demanded

target_rule.text: Target the stupidly obvious draw on liquidity (e.g., a major swing high or low).
target_rule.quote: the draw on liquidity should be so stupidly obvious

presenter_claims.claim: In those high probability conditions you might have a win rate of maybe 80 90% with crazy returns.
If you know when to trade you are ahead of 99% of your competition.

strategies.notes: Conditions filter, not an entry model. Procedure: apply the 10-second rule (1 minute maximum) to the draw on liquidity; require clear one-sidedness (arguments for one direction only); skip pre-news and post-expansion states; state an if/then demand of price and act only when price meets it exactly. The one-sided bias is the presenter's, not the engine structure bias.

setup_walkthrough.what_happens: Price is rising above a previous high. The presenter highlights that there are absolutely no bearish arguments—no bearish FVGs, no sweeps, and no order blocks lower.
Because 100% of arguments are bullish, the draw on liquidity higher becomes 'stupidly obvious,' making this a high-probability condition.

signals_observed.bias_source: Rejection from a Weekly FVG and Mitigation Block overlap.

setup_walkthrough.what_happens: Price trades into a Weekly FVG that perfectly overlaps with a mitigation block, followed immediately by a huge rejection downwards.
Following the heavy rejection, the subsequent price action clearly wants to trade toward the protective swing low.

examples.presenter_commentary: He uses USDCAD to show how high-probability conditions occur when the draw on liquidity is unquestionable. After rejecting from the Weekly FVG and mitigation block overlap, there is no confusion that the swing low is the target.

custom_signals_observed.name: failed_rejection
custom_signals_observed.presenter_calls_it: don't see a rejection lower we slowly climb higher

setup_walkthrough.what_happens: Price sweeps the draw on liquidity low. The presenter expects the overlapping order block and FVG to immediately reject price lower.
Instead of rejecting, price fails to follow through and slowly climbs higher, leading to seek-and-destroy conditions.
The presenter evaluates the arguments: overall bearish (70%) but failing to drop (30% bullish). This lack of 100% one-sidedness makes it a low probability 50/50 environment.

examples.presenter_commentary: He uses the Dollar chart to highlight what a 50/50 bias looks like in real time. Because price failed to aggressively reject off the PD array and instead began to chop slowly upwards, the conditions devolved into 'seek and destroy,' making it a market to avoid.

may_differ.reason: Traidle requires specific velocity or displacement measurements; a 'slow climb' is qualitative unless strictly defined by consecutive small-body candles.

setup_walkthrough.what_happens: A major expansion occurs, taking out a major draw on liquidity to the left.
The presenter identifies this as an immediate low probability condition. Taking shorts is chasing price, and taking longs is prematurely calling a bottom.
The trader must wait for clear bullish price action to form on a 4-hour timeframe or above before trading again.

examples.presenter_commentary: The presenter warns heavily against trading immediately after a major draw on liquidity has been met. He emphasizes that 'chasing price' or 'calling a bottom' in these moments forces trades in low probability conditions.
